uncited: This family defines the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) architectures used to map encoded 3D spatial coordinates and viewing directions to volume density and RGB color in differentiable volume rendering.
It solves the problem of representing continuous radiance fields as differentiable functions.

What sets this family apart from sibling methods like [Voxel and Grid Representations](18218-voxel-and-grid-representations.md) or [Triplane and Planar Representations](18410-triplane-and-planar-representations.md) is the exclusive reliance on fully-connected layers to process high-dimensional positional encodings, rather than convolutional or sparse grid structures.

It builds on [Model Architecture and Encoding](13550-model-architecture-and-encoding.md) by defining the specific layer configurations, branching strategies, and activation functions used to predict field properties.

The core mechanism involves transforming low-dimensional input coordinates into a high-dimensional feature space using sinusoidal positional encoding, which is then processed by a fully-connected MLP to predict radiance field properties.
where $L$ is the number of frequency bands .
The radiance field is represented by an MLP that takes the encoded position and direction as input.
**Density Branch:** Processes the encoded position features to predict volume density $\sigma$.
Rendering requires sampling points along camera rays.

The standard MLP architecture for radiance fields was introduced in the original NeRF paper  (Mildenhall et al., 2020), establishing the two-branch density/color structure with sinusoidal positional encoding.
